learn.hook: Your toy box is full of secret shapes! A ball, a dice and a party cap are all maths shapes.
points: Solid things that we can hold are 3D shapes.
A ball or a laddoo is a sphere. A dice is a cube.
A brick or a matchbox is a cuboid. A round candle is a cylinder.
A birthday cap or an ice-cream cone is a cone.

example.q: Aisha's toy rocket has a pointed top and a long round body. Which shapes are these?
steps: The pointed top is like a birthday cap, so it is a cone.
The long round body with flat round ends is a cylinder.
example.answer: A cone on top of a cylinder

learn.reallife: Look around the kitchen: a laddoo is a sphere, a matchbox is a cuboid and a steel dabba with a round lid is often a cylinder.

games.title: Match the toy to its shape

quiz.q: A cricket ball is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A ball is round all over with no flat part. That shape is a sphere.
steps: A cricket ball is round all over.
It has no flat part and no corner.
A shape round all over is a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a sphere with a cylinder because both are round

quiz.q: Which shape is a ludo dice?
quiz.explain: A dice has 6 square faces that are all the same size. That is a cube.
steps: All 6 faces are squares of the same size.
A shape with 6 same square faces is a cube.
quiz.mistake: Calls every box shape a cuboid without checking if all faces are squares

quiz.q: A round candle stands on a flat round end. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: It has two flat round ends and a curved side, just like a cylinder.
steps: The candle has two flat round ends.
Two flat round ends + a curved side = cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything round must be a sphere

quiz.q: A birthday party cap is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: It has one round edge at the bottom and a pointed tip at the top. That is a cone.
steps: A party cap has a round edge at the bottom.
It has a pointed tip at the top.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a cone and a cylinder

quiz.q: Which of these is shaped like a cuboid?
quiz.explain: A brick is a box shape with 6 flat rectangle faces. That is a cuboid.
steps: A cuboid is a box shape with 6 flat rectangle faces.
A brick is a box shape like that.
A laddoo and a marble are spheres. An ice-cream cone is a cone.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name for a box shape

quiz.q: Which object is NOT shaped like a sphere?
quiz.explain: A dice has flat square faces and corners, so it is a cube, not a sphere.
steps: Look for the one that is NOT round all over.
A football, a laddoo and an orange are spheres.
A dice has flat square faces and corners. It is a cube.
quiz.mistake: Misses the word NOT in the question

quiz.q: Meena's toy rocket has a cone on top of a cylinder. Which part is the pointed top?
quiz.explain: A cone has a pointed tip, so the pointed top is the cone.
steps: The rocket has a cone on top of a cylinder.
A cone has a pointed tip. A cylinder has flat round ends.
So the pointed top is the cone.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder can have a pointed end

quiz.q: How many of these are spheres: a ball, a marble, a brick, a globe?
quiz.explain: The ball, the marble and the globe are round all over. The brick is a cuboid. So 3 are spheres.
quiz.mistake: Counts the brick too

teach.ask: Gappu found a ball, a dice and a party cap. He thinks they are all the same shape! Can you tell him their names?
teach.praise: Sphere, cube, cone! Now I know my toy shapes!
teach.nudge: What is the name of the pointed party cap shape?

revise.summary: Solid things we can hold are 3D shapes. A ball is a sphere, a dice is a cube, a brick is a cuboid, a candle is a cylinder and a party cap is a cone.
focus: Name the shape of everyday objects and toys.
Tell a cube from a cuboid, and a cone from a cylinder.
Find the shapes in a toy made of many parts.
remember: Sphere: ball, laddoo. Cube: dice.
Cuboid: brick, matchbox. Cylinder: round candle.
Cone: birthday cap, ice-cream cone.
traps: Not every round thing is a sphere. A candle is a cylinder.
Don't mix up a cone (pointed tip) and a cylinder (two flat round ends).
Read NOT in the question carefully.

learn.hook: An old toothpaste box can become a crocodile! What can your empty bottle become?
points: Old boxes, cans and bottles can be turned into animal and bird toys.
We draw eyes and faces on the FLAT faces of a box. Drawing is easy on a flat face.
A can or bottle has a curved surface too. We can draw on it carefully, but it rolls.
In a toy shop, look for shapes: a ball is a sphere, a drum is a cylinder, blocks are cubes and cuboids.
Stacking boxes, cans and cones, we can build houses, towers and rockets.

example.q: Raju wants to draw a tiger face on a shoe box. How many flat faces can he choose from?
steps: A shoe box is a cuboid.

learn.reallife: Many craft fairs sell toys made from waste, like pen stands from tins and owls from bottles.

games.title: Build and draw
items: A flat face of a box is good for drawing a face.
A flat face does not roll away and is easy to draw on.
A cone can sit steadily on its pointed tip at the bottom of a tower.
A cone balances only on its flat round face.
A cylinder can be used as the body of a rocket.
Many toy rockets use a cylinder body with a cone on top.
A sphere has a flat face for drawing.
A sphere has only a curved surface.
Cuboid boxes stack well to make a house.
Their flat faces sit firmly on each other.

quiz.q: Which object would make the best flat 'face' to draw a cat on?
quiz.explain: A matchbox is a cuboid with flat faces. Balls, marbles and oranges are round with no flat face.
steps: Answer: The side of a matchbox
quiz.mistake: Thinks round things have flat faces

quiz.q: A juice can is a cylinder. How many flat faces does it have?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has 2 flat round faces, at the top and the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the bottom face

quiz.q: Sunita wants to make a tall rocket. Which shape is best for the pointed top?
quiz.explain: A cone has a pointed tip, just like the nose of a rocket.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape without a point

quiz.q: In a toy shop, which toy is shaped like a sphere?
quiz.explain: A marble is perfectly round like a ball, so it is a sphere.
steps: A sphere is round all over, like a ball.
A dice is a cube. A toy drum is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a cylinder drum with a sphere

quiz.q: Which is NOT a good base at the bottom of a tower?
quiz.explain: A ball has no flat face, so it rolls and the tower falls.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape can hold a tower

quiz.q: Jaya's house model uses a cuboid box for walls and a cone for the roof. What shape is the roof?
quiz.explain: The question tells us the roof is a cone.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the walls and the roof

quiz.q: Imran built a tower with 3 cubes and 2 cylinders. How many objects did he use?
quiz.explain: 3 + 2 = 5 objects.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one kind of shape

quiz.q: A toothpaste box is a cuboid. Faces can be drawn on how many of its faces?
quiz.explain: All 6 faces of a cuboid are flat, so we can draw on any of them.
steps: A toothpaste box is a cuboid.
A cuboid has 6 flat faces: top, bottom, front, back, 2 sides.
We can draw on any flat face.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the big faces

teach.ask: Gappu found an empty box and a bottle. How can he make a toy bird from them?
teach.praise: I drew eyes on the flat face of the box! Look, a parrot! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Where on the box is it easiest to draw the eyes?

revise.summary: Old boxes, cans and bottles can become toys. We draw faces on the flat faces of a box. A can or bottle has a curved surface and rolls.
focus: Find the flat faces of a box to draw on.
Spot shapes in a toy shop: ball, drum, blocks.
Stack boxes, cans and cones to build models.
remember: A cuboid box has 6 flat faces.
Ball = sphere. Drum = cylinder. Blocks = cubes and cuboids.
traps: Don't forget the bottom face when counting faces.
A toy drum is a cylinder, not a sphere.
Round things do not have only flat faces.

learn.hook: Jaya's rocket has a cone, cylinders and cubes. Can you count them all?
points: A model is made of many shapes. We count how many of each shape it uses.
Make a table: shape name and how many.
A house model has flat faces for walls and straight edges where the walls meet.
From far away, we see the tallest or biggest part of a model first, like the top of a rocket.
We can count parts by shape and also by colour, like in Devika's toy engine.

example.q: A rocket has 1 cone, 2 cylinders and 4 cubes. How many parts in all?

learn.reallife: Architects plan buildings by counting blocks, pillars and domes, just like counting shapes in a model.

items.q: Engine: 3 red cylinders, 2 blue cubes. Parts?

items.text: Two walls of a box meet at a straight ___
A wall of a cuboid house is a flat ___
From far away we first see the ___ part

quiz.q: Devika's engine has 4 red cylinders and 3 yellow cubes. How many parts does it have?
quiz.explain: 4 + 3 = 7 parts.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: Same engine: 4 red cylinders and 3 yellow cubes. How many more cylinders than cubes?
quiz.explain: 4 − 3 = 1 more cylinder.
steps: How many more means take away.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total instead

quiz.q: A rocket model: 1 cone on top, 2 cylinders in the middle, 3 cones as fins. How many cones in all?
quiz.explain: 1 cone on top + 3 cone fins = 4 cones.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the top cone

quiz.q: A house model is a cuboid with a cone roof. Where do two walls of the cuboid meet?
quiz.explain: Two flat faces of a cuboid meet along a straight edge.
steps: They meet at a straight edge
quiz.mistake: Thinks faces meet at a point only

quiz.q: A tall rocket model stands in the playground. Which part will Sameer see first from far away?
options: The cone at the very top
quiz.explain: The top of a tall model can be seen from far, over other things.
steps: From far away, we see the tallest part first.
The tallest part of a rocket is the very top.
The top of this rocket is a cone.
Answer: The cone at the very top
quiz.mistake: Thinks small parts are seen first

quiz.q: Which part of a cuboid house model is a flat face?
quiz.explain: Each wall is a flat face of the cuboid.
steps: A face is a flat surface.
An edge is a line and a corner is a point.
A wall of the house is flat, so it is a face.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up face, edge and corner

quiz.q: A toy train has 3 cuboid coaches. Each coach has 4 cylinder wheels. How many wheels in all?
quiz.explain: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 wheels.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 4

quiz.q: A model uses 2 cubes, 3 cuboids and 1 sphere. Which shape is used the most?
quiz.explain: Cuboids: 3. Cubes 2 and sphere 1. So cuboid is used most.
steps: The biggest count is 3, for cuboids.
quiz.mistake: Picks the first shape listed

teach.ask: Gappu built a robot from boxes and cans. How can he tell his friends what it is made of?
teach.praise: I made a table: 2 cuboids, 4 cylinders, 1 sphere! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many of each shape did I use?

revise.summary: A model is made of many shapes. We count how many of each shape it uses and write them in a table.
focus: Count each shape in a model and make a table.
Add to find all the parts. Take away to find how many more.
Name faces, edges and corners in a house model.
remember: Rocket: 1 cone + 2 cylinders + 4 cubes = 7 parts.
Walls are flat faces. Edges are where walls meet.
From far away we see the tallest part first.
traps: Don't forget a part, like the top cone.
Don't add when the question asks how many more.
Don't pick the first shape listed. Pick the biggest count.

learn.hook: Can your friend build your tower without seeing it? Only your words can help!
points: Position words tell where a shape is: on top of, under, between, beside, in front of, behind.
Build with three shapes, then describe each step: 'First the cube. Then the cylinder on top of the cube.'
Your friend listens and builds the same model without looking.
Use clear words in the right order so the copy matches the model.

example.q: Model: cuboid at the bottom, cube on top of it, cone on top of the cube. What is between the cuboid and the cone?
steps: Bottom: cuboid. Middle: cube. Top: cone.
The middle one is between the other two.

learn.reallife: When you tell a friend the way to your house, you use words like 'next to the temple' and 'behind the school'.

games.title: Build it from the bottom
games.prompt: Cylinder is under the cube. Cone is on top of the cube.

games.title: Position talk
items: In a stack, the shape under the cone is below it.
Between means in the middle of two things.
Clear steps help a friend rebuild a model without seeing it.
'On top of' and 'under' mean the same.
The first shape we place usually goes at the bottom.
We build a stack from the bottom up.

quiz.q: A ball is on top of a box. Where is the box?
quiz.explain: If the ball is on top, the box is under it.
steps: The ball is on top of the box.
So the box is below the ball.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the same position word

quiz.q: Stack from bottom: cuboid, cylinder, cone. Which shape is between the other two?
quiz.explain: The cylinder is in the middle, between the cuboid and the cone.
steps: From the bottom: cuboid, cylinder, cone.
Bottom = cuboid, middle = cylinder, top = cone.
The middle shape is between the other two.
quiz.mistake: Picks the top or bottom shape

quiz.q: Same stack (cuboid, cylinder, cone from bottom). Which shape is at the top?
quiz.explain: The last shape in the list from the bottom is at the top: the cone.
steps: The list goes from bottom to top: cuboid, cylinder, cone.
The last one in the list is at the top.
quiz.mistake: Reads the list from the top

quiz.q: Leela says: 'Put the cube down. Put the cylinder on top of the cube. Put the sphere on top of the cylinder.' Which shape touches the floor?
quiz.explain: The cube was put down first, so it is at the bottom on the floor.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the last shape is at the bottom

quiz.q: In Leela's model (cube, then cylinder, then sphere), what is under the sphere?
quiz.explain: The sphere sits on the cylinder, so the cylinder is under it.
steps: Leela's model from bottom: cube, cylinder, sphere.
The sphere sits on the cylinder.
So the cylinder is under the sphere.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'under' means the very bottom

quiz.q: Which instruction is the CLEAREST for a friend who cannot see your model?
options: Put the cone on top of the red cube
quiz.explain: It names the shape and says exactly where it goes.
steps: Answer: Put the cone on top of the red cube
quiz.mistake: Uses words like 'that' and 'there' that do not tell enough

quiz.q: Arun says: 'Put a cube between two cylinders, one on each side.' How many shapes is that?
quiz.explain: Two cylinders + one cube = 3 shapes.
steps: Two cylinders, one on each side = 2
quiz.mistake: Counts only the cylinders

quiz.q: Ria's friend built a cone under a cube, but Ria's model had the cone on top. What went wrong?
options: The friend mixed up 'on top of' and 'under'
quiz.explain: The positions are swapped, so the friend mixed up the two words.
steps: Ria's model: cone on top of the cube.
Friend's model: cone under the cube.
The positions are swapped. On top and under got mixed up.
Answer: The friend mixed up 'on top of' and 'under'
quiz.mistake: Thinks the order does not matter

teach.ask: Gappu built a tower: box, can, then a cap on top. How should he tell his friend to build the same one?
teach.praise: First the box, then the can on top, then the cap on top of the can! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which shape do I put down first, and what goes on top of it?

revise.summary: Position words tell where a shape is: on top of, under, between, beside, in front of, behind. Clear words in the right order help a friend copy a model.
focus: Use on top of, under and between correctly.
Read a stack from the bottom up.
Give clear building steps in order.
remember: If the ball is on top of the box, the box is under the ball.
The middle shape is between the other two.
traps: Don't read a 'from bottom' list from the top.
Don't mix up 'on top of' and 'under'.
Words like 'that' and 'there' do not tell enough.

learn.hook: Run your finger along a dice and then along a ball. What feels different?
points: Cubes and cuboids have only flat faces and straight edges.
A sphere has only a curved surface. A cylinder and a cone have flat faces and a curved surface.
We can sort shapes into 'straight edges only' and 'has a curved surface'.
A cube is a special cuboid: all its 6 faces are squares of the same size.
In a picture, we can mark each kind: for example, circle the cubes, tick the cones, cross the cylinders, box the cuboids.

example.q: Is every cube a cuboid? Is every cuboid a cube?
steps: A cube's faces are squares, which are special rectangles.
A long matchbox is a cuboid, but its faces are not all squares.
example.answer: Every cube is a cuboid, but not every cuboid is a cube

learn.reallife: Furniture makers choose rounded table edges for small children so that they are safe.

quiz.q: Which shape has only straight edges?
quiz.explain: A cuboid has 12 straight edges and no curved surface.
steps: A cone, sphere and cylinder each have a curved surface.
A cuboid has only flat faces and straight edges.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder has straight edges only

quiz.q: Which shape has a curved surface AND flat faces?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has 2 flat round faces and 1 curved surface.
steps: We need both a curved surface and flat faces.
A cuboid and a cube have only flat faces. A sphere has only a curved surface.
A cylinder has 2 flat round faces and 1 curved surface.
quiz.mistake: Picks the sphere, which has no flat face

quiz.q: What makes a cube special among cuboids?
options: All its faces are equal squares
quiz.explain: A cube is a cuboid whose 6 faces are all squares of the same size.
steps: Answer: All its faces are equal squares
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cube has more faces

quiz.q: Which is TRUE?
quiz.explain: A cube has all the features of a cuboid, with square faces. A long box is a cuboid but not a cube.
steps: Every cube is a special cuboid
Not every cuboid is a cube
Answer: Every cube is a cuboid
quiz.mistake: Reverses the rule

quiz.q: In a picture: ball, dice, brick, tin, cap. How many have a curved surface?
quiz.explain: Ball, tin and cap have curved surfaces. Dice and brick do not.
quiz.mistake: Counts the dice as curved

quiz.q: Following the rule 'tick the cones', which object gets a tick?
quiz.explain: A birthday cap is shaped like a cone.
steps: A birthday cap is shaped like a cone.
A brick is a cuboid, a laddoo is a sphere, a pipe is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Ticks a sphere instead

quiz.q: A picture has 3 dice, 2 bricks and 4 tins. How many shapes have ONLY straight edges?
quiz.explain: Dice (cubes) and bricks (cuboids) have straight edges only: 3 + 2 = 5.
steps: Dice are cubes. Bricks are cuboids. Both have only straight edges.
Tins are cylinders. They have a curved surface, so leave them out.
quiz.mistake: Adds the tins too

quiz.q: Rahul's box has square faces on two ends and long rectangles on four sides. What is it?
options: A cuboid but not a cube
quiz.explain: Not all its faces are squares, so it is a cuboid, not a cube.
steps: A cube needs all 6 faces to be squares.
This box has 2 square faces and 4 long rectangle faces.
So it is a cuboid, but not a cube.
Answer: A cuboid but not a cube
quiz.mistake: Calls it a cube because some faces are squares

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a cube and a cuboid are totally different. Can you help him?
teach.praise: So a cube is a cuboid with all square faces! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What is special about the faces of a cube?

revise.summary: Cubes and cuboids have only flat faces and straight edges. A sphere has only a curved surface. A cylinder and a cone have flat faces and a curved surface.
focus: Sort shapes into 'straight edges only' and 'has a curved surface'.
Know that every cube is a cuboid, but not every cuboid is a cube.
Mark shapes in a picture by a rule.
remember: Straight edges only: cube, cuboid.
Curved surface: sphere, cylinder, cone.
A cube has 6 square faces of the same size.
traps: A cylinder does not have straight edges only.
Some square faces don't make a cube. All 6 must be squares.
Tins (cylinders) are not straight-edged shapes.

learn.hook: Look around your classroom. How many cuboids can you spot in one minute?
points: Many classroom things are 3D shapes: a duster is a cuboid, a globe is a sphere, a chalk stick is a cylinder.
Make a list of things and their shapes, then count how many of each.
The shape with the biggest count is the most common. The smallest count is the least common.
Some objects are made of more than one shape, like a pencil: a cylinder with a cone tip.

example.q: Classroom list: 6 cuboids, 3 cylinders, 1 sphere, 2 cones. Which is most and least common?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers stack cuboid boxes on shelves because they fit together with no gaps.

quiz.q: What shape is a duster?
quiz.explain: A duster is a box-like block: a cuboid.
steps: A duster is a box-like block.
A box shape with rectangle faces is a cuboid.
quiz.mistake: Calls every box a cube

quiz.q: What shape is a classroom globe?
quiz.explain: A globe is round all over, a sphere.
steps: A globe is round all over, like a ball.
A shape round all over is a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the flat map

quiz.q: A sharpened pencil is made of which two shapes?
quiz.explain: The long body is a cylinder and the pointed tip is a cone.
quiz.mistake: Names only one shape

quiz.q: Shapes found: cuboid 8, cylinder 5, sphere 2, cone 3. Which is most common?
quiz.explain: 8 is the biggest count.
quiz.mistake: Picks the shape listed second

quiz.q: Same list (8, 5, 2, 3). Which is least common?
quiz.explain: 2 is the smallest count, for the sphere.
quiz.mistake: Picks the most common

quiz.q: Same list (8, 5, 2, 3). How many objects were found in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one shape

quiz.q: Which object is made of MORE than one shape?
options: An ice-cream cone with a scoop on top
quiz.explain: The cone holds a round scoop: a cone and a sphere.
steps: A brick, a dice and a marble are each one shape.
An ice-cream cone with a scoop has a cone and a round scoop.
Answer: An ice-cream cone with a scoop on top
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the cone alone

quiz.q: Cuboids 8 and cylinders 5. How many more cuboids than cylinders?
quiz.explain: 8 − 5 = 3 more cuboids.
steps: How many more means take away.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find the most common shape in his nest. What should he do?
teach.praise: List, count, and the biggest count wins! Chirp!
teach.nudge: After naming the shapes, what do I do?

revise.summary: Many classroom things are 3D shapes. We list them, count each shape and find the most and least common.
focus: Name the shapes of classroom things.
Find the most common (biggest count) and least common (smallest count).
Spot objects made of more than one shape.
remember: Duster = cuboid. Globe = sphere. Chalk stick = cylinder.
A pencil is a cylinder with a cone tip.
traps: Don't call every box a cube.
A globe is a sphere, not a flat map.
Don't add when asked how many more.

learn.hook: Run your finger over a dice. Flat parts, sharp lines, pointy tips - each one has a name!
points: A face is a flat surface of a solid shape.
An edge is a line where two faces meet.
A corner is a point where edges meet.
A cube and a cuboid each have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A sphere has no flat face, no edge and no corner.

example.q: How many faces does a matchbox (a cuboid) have?

learn.reallife: When you wrap a gift box for Raksha Bandhan, you cover all 6 faces of the box with paper.

games.title: Shape detective
items: A cube has top, bottom, front, back, left and right: 6 square faces.
A sphere is round all over. It has no corners at all.
An edge is where two faces meet.
The line where two flat faces join is called an edge.
A cylinder has a flat circle at the top and one at the bottom.
A cone has just 1 pointed tip.
Like a cube, a cuboid has 4 corners on top and 4 at the bottom.

quiz.q: How many faces does a cube have?
quiz.explain: Top, bottom, front, back, left and right: a cube has 6 square faces.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the faces that can be seen at one time

quiz.q: How many corners does a cube have?
quiz.explain: A cube has 4 corners on the top and 4 corners on the bottom. 4 + 4 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up corners with faces

quiz.q: How many edges does a cube have?
quiz.explain: 4 edges go round the top, 4 go round the bottom and 4 stand up at the sides. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up edges with corners

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has a flat circle on top and a flat circle at the bottom. Its side is curved, not flat.
steps: A cylinder has a flat circle on top.
It has a flat circle at the bottom.
Its side is curved, not flat.
quiz.mistake: Counts the curved side as a flat face

quiz.q: Which shape has no flat face, no edge and no corner?
quiz.explain: A sphere is round all over, like a ball. It has nothing flat, no edge and no corner.
steps: A cone has a flat face. A cylinder has flat faces. A cube has faces, edges and corners.
A sphere is round all over, like a ball.
It has no flat face, no edge and no corner.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder has no faces because it is round

quiz.q: How many pointed corners does a cone have?
quiz.explain: A cone has only one pointed tip at the top.
steps: A cone has only one pointed tip, at the top.
Its round bottom edge has no corners.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the round bottom edge has corners

quiz.q: A matchbox is a cuboid. How many faces does it have?
quiz.explain: A cuboid, like a cube, has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back and two sides.
steps: Top and bottom: 2. Front and back: 2. Two sides: 2.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the bottom face that sits on the table

quiz.q: Riya traces round the flat face of a cylinder on paper. What shape does she draw?
quiz.explain: The flat faces of a cylinder are round, so the tracing is a circle.
steps: The flat faces of a cylinder are round.
Tracing round a round face gives a circle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the side view of the cylinder instead of its flat face

teach.ask: Gappu is holding a dice. He asks: what are faces, edges and corners?
teach.praise: Flat faces, straight edges, pointy corners! My dice makes sense now!
teach.nudge: Which part of the dice is the corner? And what is an edge?

revise.summary: A face is a flat surface, an edge is where two faces meet and a corner is where edges meet. A cube and a cuboid have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
focus: Count faces, edges and corners of solid shapes.
Know which shapes have no flat face or corner.
Trace a flat face to see its shape.
remember: Cube and cuboid: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 corners.
Cylinder: 2 flat round faces. Cone: 1 pointed corner.
Sphere: no flat face, no edge, no corner.
traps: Don't count only the faces you can see. Count the bottom too.
A curved side is not a flat face.
Don't mix up edges and corners.

learn.hook: Turn a dice upside down. Is it still a cube? Of course! Shapes stay the same when turned.
points: Opposite faces face away from each other, like the top and bottom of a box.
A cube and a cuboid have 3 pairs of opposite faces. A cylinder has 1 pair: its two round faces.
A shape keeps its name when we turn it or lay it down. A cylinder lying down is still a cylinder.
To compare two shapes, say how they are alike and how they are different.

example.q: Compare a cube and a cylinder.
steps: Alike: both have flat faces; both can be stacked.
Different: a cube has 6 square faces and no curved surface; a cylinder has 2 round faces and a curved surface.
example.answer: Both have flat faces; only the cylinder has a curved surface

learn.reallife: When you open a cupboard, the door and the back wall are opposite faces of the cupboard.

games.title: Turn and compare
items: A cone turned upside down is still a cone.
Turning does not change a shape.
A cylinder lying on its side becomes a cuboid.
A cuboid has 3 pairs of opposite faces.
A sphere has opposite flat faces.
A sphere has no flat face.
A cube and a cuboid both have 6 faces.
That is one way they are alike.

games.title: How many pairs of opposite faces?

quiz.q: How many pairs of opposite faces does a cube have?
quiz.explain: Top-bottom, front-back and left-right: 3 pairs.
quiz.mistake: Counts faces instead of pairs

quiz.q: Which faces of a cylinder are opposite each other?
options: The curved surface and a round face
quiz.explain: The top and bottom round faces face away from each other.
steps: Opposite faces face away from each other.
A cylinder has a round face on top and one at the bottom.
These two round faces are opposite.
Answer: The two round flat faces
quiz.mistake: Thinks the curved surface has an opposite

quiz.q: A tin can is lying on its side. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: Turning a shape does not change it. It is still a cylinder.
steps: A tin can is a cylinder.
Turning or lying a shape down does not change it.
So it is still a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shape changes when turned

quiz.q: A cone is standing on its tip. What is it?
quiz.explain: Upside down, it is still a cone.
steps: A cone turned upside down is the same shape.
A shape keeps its name when we turn it.
quiz.mistake: Gets confused by the new position

quiz.q: How are a cube and a cuboid ALIKE?
quiz.explain: Both have 6 flat faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
quiz.mistake: Thinks they are alike in rolling

quiz.q: How is a cone DIFFERENT from a cylinder?
options: A cylinder has a pointed tip
A cone has 1 flat face, a cylinder has 2
A cone has no curved surface
quiz.explain: A cone has 1 round flat face and a tip. A cylinder has 2 round flat faces.
steps: Answer: A cone has 1 flat face, a cylinder has 2
quiz.mistake: Forgets that both have a curved surface

quiz.q: A shoebox is lying on the floor. Its bottom face touches the floor. Which face is opposite to it?
quiz.explain: The top lid faces away from the bottom face. They are opposite.
steps: The bottom face touches the floor.
The face that faces away from it is the top face.
Side and front faces are next to the bottom, not opposite.
quiz.mistake: Picks a face that is next to it

quiz.q: How many faces of a cuboid are NOT opposite to the top face?
quiz.explain: 6 faces: the top, its opposite (bottom), and 4 others. 6 − 2 = 4.
steps: Top and bottom are a pair
quiz.mistake: Counts the bottom as well

teach.ask: Gappu turned his cube upside down and thinks it is a new shape! What would you tell him?
teach.praise: Oh! It is still a cube, just turned! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Does turning change the shape's name?

revise.summary: Opposite faces face away from each other, like the top and bottom of a box. A shape keeps its name when we turn it.
focus: Find opposite faces of a cube, cuboid and cylinder.
Name a shape even when it is turned or lying down.
Say how two shapes are alike and different.
remember: Cube and cuboid: 3 pairs of opposite faces.
Cylinder: 1 pair, its two round faces.
A cylinder lying down is still a cylinder.
traps: Don't count faces when asked for pairs.
Turning a shape does not change its name.
A face next to another is not opposite it.

learn.hook: Why does a ball run away but a dice stays put? Let's find out!
points: Shapes with a curved surface can roll. A sphere rolls in every direction.
Shapes with a flat face can slide. A cube and a cuboid slide but do not roll.
A cylinder and a cone can roll and can also slide on a flat face.
Shapes with flat faces are easy to stack, so cubes make strong towers.

example.q: Kabir wants to build the tallest tower. Should he use balls or dice?
steps: Balls have no flat face, so they roll off each other.
Dice have flat faces, so one sits firmly on another.
example.answer: Dice, because flat faces stack well.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers stack cuboid boxes on shelves, but they keep oranges in baskets so they do not roll away.

items.text: A dice can ___ but not roll.
A shape needs a ___ face to slide.
A shape needs a ___ surface to roll.

quiz.q: Which shape can only roll and cannot slide on its face?
quiz.explain: A sphere has no flat face at all, so it can only roll.
steps: A shape slides on a flat face.
A sphere has no flat face at all.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder can only roll and forgets its flat faces

quiz.q: Which shape slides but does not roll?
quiz.explain: A cube has only flat faces and no curved surface, so it slides but cannot roll.
steps: A shape rolls on a curved surface.
A cube has only flat faces and no curved surface.
So it slides but cannot roll.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape can roll if you push it hard

quiz.q: What can a cylinder do on a flat floor?
quiz.explain: On its curved side a cylinder rolls. Standing on a flat face, it slides.
steps: Lying on its curved side, a cylinder rolls.
Standing on a flat round face, it slides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of only one way the cylinder can lie

quiz.q: Which toys are easiest to stack into a tall tower?
quiz.explain: Cubes have flat faces on every side, so each one sits firmly on the one below.
steps: Shapes with flat faces stack well.
Cubes have flat faces on every side.
Marbles and balls roll off. Cones have a point.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about whether faces are flat

quiz.q: Why can a tin can roll?
quiz.explain: Things roll on curved surfaces. A tin can's side is curved, so it rolls.
steps: Things roll on a curved surface.
The side of a tin can is curved.
Answer: It has a curved surface
quiz.mistake: Thinks weight makes things roll

quiz.q: Kabir stands a cone on its pointed tip at the bottom of a tower. What happens?
options: The cone turns into a cube
quiz.explain: A tip is just a point, so the cone cannot balance on it. The tower topples.
steps: A tip is just a point.
A cone cannot balance on a point.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any face or tip can hold up a tower

quiz.q: A toy train has 4 coaches. Each coach has 4 round wheels. How many wheels do the coaches have?
quiz.explain: 4 coaches with 4 wheels each: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16 wheels.
quiz.mistake: Adds only 4 + 4 for the coaches and wheels

quiz.q: A clown toy has a sphere head, a cylinder body and a cone hat. How many DIFFERENT shapes are used?
quiz.explain: Sphere, cylinder and cone are three different shapes.
steps: List the shapes: sphere head, cylinder body, cone hat.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count one of the parts

teach.ask: Gappu's ball keeps rolling away but his dice stays still. Why?
teach.praise: Curved things roll, flat things slide! I will stack my dice now.
teach.nudge: What is different about the ball's surface and the dice's faces?

revise.summary: Shapes with a curved surface can roll. Shapes with a flat face can slide. Flat faces make shapes easy to stack.
focus: Say which shapes roll, slide or do both.
Choose the best shapes for a tall tower.
Explain why a tower falls over.
remember: Sphere: only rolls. Cube and cuboid: only slide.
Cylinder and cone: roll and slide.
Dice stack well because of flat faces.
traps: Don't forget a cylinder can also slide on its flat face.
Weight does not make things roll. A curved surface does.
A cone cannot balance on its tip.

learn.hook: With just 3 little cubes, how many different shapes can you make?
points: Unit cubes are small cubes of the same size. We join them face to face to make models.
Some drawn shapes cannot be built, like a cube floating in the air with nothing under it.
To copy a model, count the cubes in each row and layer.
We can work out the order: the bottom cubes must be placed before the cubes on top.
3 cubes can be joined in 2 ways (flat on a table): in a straight line, or bent like the letter L.

example.q: A model has 4 cubes in a row and 2 cubes on top. How many cubes are used?

learn.reallife: Builders lay the bottom row of bricks first, then build upwards, row by row.

games.title: Build order
games.prompt: A tower of three cubes: red at the bottom, blue in the middle, green on top
items: Put the blue cube on the red one
Put the green cube on the blue one

quiz.q: A model is a row of 3 cubes with 1 cube on top of the middle cube. How many cubes?
quiz.explain: 3 in the row + 1 on top = 4 cubes.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the row

quiz.q: Which model CANNOT be built with real cubes?
options: A cube floating above the table with nothing below
quiz.explain: A cube needs something under it. It cannot float in the air.
steps: Every real cube must rest on something.
A tower, two cubes side by side and an L can all be built.
A cube cannot float with nothing below it.
Answer: A cube floating above the table with nothing below
quiz.mistake: Thinks any drawing can be built

quiz.q: A tower has 5 cubes. Which cube was placed FIRST?
quiz.explain: We build from the bottom up, so the bottom cube goes first.
steps: We build a tower from the bottom up.
The bottom cube must be placed before the cubes on top.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the top is placed first

quiz.q: How many different ways can 3 cubes be joined flat on a table, face to face?
quiz.explain: Straight in a line, or bent into an L. Turning the L gives the same shape.
quiz.mistake: Counts turned copies as new shapes

quiz.q: A model has 2 layers. Each layer has 3 cubes. How many cubes in all?
quiz.explain: 3 + 3 = 6 cubes.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 3

quiz.q: To build a 2-cube-high wall with 4 cubes in each row, how many cubes are needed?
quiz.explain: 2 rows of 4 is 4 + 4 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one row

quiz.q: Ravi has 10 cubes. He uses 7 to build a model. How many are left?
quiz.explain: 10 − 7 = 3 cubes left.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away

quiz.q: A model has one cube on top of another cube, and a third cube on the table beside the bottom one. Which cube can be placed ONLY after the bottom cube is in place?
quiz.explain: The top cube rests on the bottom cube, so the bottom cube must be placed first. The side cube sits on the table, so it can be placed at any time.
steps: Top cube rests on the bottom cube
Side cube rests on the table
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bottom cube can be placed last

teach.ask: Gappu has 3 tiny cubes. How many shapes can he make, and how would he copy a friend's model?
teach.praise: A line and an L! And I build from the bottom up! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What are the two shapes I can make with 3 cubes?

revise.summary: Unit cubes are joined face to face to make models. Count the cubes in each row and layer. Bottom cubes go first.
focus: Count the cubes in a model.
Spot models that cannot be built.
Work out the building order.
remember: 4 cubes in a row + 2 on top = 6 cubes.
3 cubes flat on a table join in 2 ways: a straight line or an L.
A cube cannot float with nothing under it.
traps: Don't count only one row.
The top cube is not placed first.
A turned copy of a shape is not a new shape.

learn.hook: Look at a dice. The dots on opposite faces always add up to the same number. Can you find it?
points: A dice is a cube with 1 to 6 dots on its faces.
Opposite faces add up to 7: 1 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5, 3 is opposite 4.
6 dice can make a cuboid (2 rows of 3), a tall tower, or any free shape.
In board games, we roll a dice and move a counter by the number we get.

example.q: The top face of a dice shows 2. What is on the bottom face?

learn.reallife: Ludo and snakes and ladders use dice, and the 7 rule helps you guess what is underneath!

quiz.q: What number is opposite 3 on a dice?
quiz.explain: Opposite faces add to 7. 7 − 3 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the opposite of a number is itself

quiz.q: What do opposite faces of a dice always add up to?
quiz.explain: 1 + 6, 2 + 5 and 3 + 4 all make 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is the biggest number on the dice

quiz.q: A dice shows 6 on top. What is on the bottom?
steps: Top and bottom faces are opposite.
quiz.mistake: Picks the next number

quiz.q: A dice rests on the table. The top face shows 5. What is the face touching the table?
quiz.explain: The face touching the table is opposite the top. 7 − 5 = 2.
steps: The face on the table is opposite the top face.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 7 rule

quiz.q: How many dice are in a cuboid made of 2 rows of 3 dice?
quiz.explain: 3 + 3 = 6 dice.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 3

quiz.q: Gopal stacks all 6 of his dice one on top of another. What has he made?
quiz.explain: One on top of another makes a tall tower.
steps: Gopal puts 6 dice one on top of another.
Dice one above the other make a tall tower.
quiz.mistake: Thinks stacking makes a flat shape

quiz.q: In a board game, Mira is on square 4 and rolls a 5. Where does she land?
steps: Mira is on square 4. She rolls 5.
quiz.mistake: Moves to the number rolled

quiz.q: A dice shows 1 on top and 2 in front. Which number is at the back?
quiz.explain: Back is opposite the front. 7 − 2 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Uses the top number instead of the front

teach.ask: Gappu can see 3 dots on top of a dice. How can he know the number underneath without lifting it?
teach.praise: Opposite faces make 7, so it is 4 underneath! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What do the top and bottom numbers always add up to?

revise.summary: A dice is a cube with 1 to 6 dots. Opposite faces add up to 7. In board games we move by the number we roll.
focus: Find the opposite face using the 7 rule.
Make shapes with 6 dice.
Move a counter by the number rolled.
remember: 1 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5, 3 is opposite 4.
Bottom = 7 − top. Top 2 → bottom 5.
traps: The opposite of a number is not itself.
Don't forget the 7 rule.
In a game, add the roll to where you are. Don't jump to the number rolled.
